4	/// Reads and writes the saved session (issue #46) — the file behind `SessionSnapshot`.
5	///
6	/// **Every operation is best-effort.** The app must behave identically with the file absent, empty,
7	/// unreadable, or corrupt: a session that fails to load is a launch with no restore, never an error
8	/// the user sees. Failures log and are swallowed.
9	///
10	/// The URL is injectable so unit tests point at a temp directory — which also keeps the whole
11	/// feature clear of `Defaults`, and therefore clear of the single-writer rule parallel test workers
12	/// impose on a shared UserDefaults domain (`SharedPrefDefaultsTests`).
13	final class SessionStore {
14	  /// Where the file lives, **scoped by bundle id**.
15	  ///
16	  /// The scoping is mandatory, not tidiness: `GhosttyApp` already writes into
17	  /// `Application Support/Workroom/` from all three identities (Workroom, Workroom Dev, Workroom
18	  /// Nightly), so an unscoped path would let a Dev run's fixture temp-dir workrooms be restored into
19	  /// the release build. UserDefaults gets that separation free from the bundle id; a file has to buy
20	  /// it back.
21	  static func defaultURL(
22	    bundleID: String? = Bundle.main.bundleIdentifier,
23	    fileManager: FileManager = .default
24	  ) -> URL {
25	    let root = fileManager.urls(for: .applicationSupportDirectory, in: .userDomainMask)[0]
26	      .appendingPathComponent("Workroom", isDirectory: true)
27	      .appendingPathComponent(bundleID ?? "com.developwithstyle.workroom", isDirectory: true)
28	    return root.appendingPathComponent("session.json")
29	  }
30	
31	  /// The store production and the UI tests should use.
32	  ///
33	  /// In fixture mode this is a **no-op unless a test names a file**. The path is bundle-id scoped, so
34	  /// a fixture launch would otherwise write over the developer's own `Workroom Dev` session — and the
35	  /// fixture's temp-directory workrooms would then be restored into a real launch.
36	  static func forCurrentEnvironment() -> SessionStore {
37	    // Unit tests inject their own store, but `AppStore.markSessionDirty` reaches the SHARED
38	    // coordinator — so without this a `make app-test` run writes the developer's own `Workroom Dev`
39	    // session file and scrollback sidecars as a side effect of exercising tab mutations. Same
40	    // isolation the app already applies at `WorkroomApp.swift:42` and `AppStore.swift:750`.
41	    if ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["XCTestConfigurationFilePath"] != nil,
42	      UITestFixture.sessionFilePath == nil
43	    {
44	      return SessionStore(url: SessionStore.defaultURL(), isDisabled: true)
45	    }
46	    guard UITestFixture.isActive else { return SessionStore() }
47	    guard let path = UITestFixture.sessionFilePath else {
48	      return SessionStore(url: SessionStore.defaultURL(), isDisabled: true)
49	    }
50	    return SessionStore(url: URL(fileURLWithPath: path))
51	  }
52	
53	  let url: URL
54	  /// A disabled store reads nothing and writes nothing — fixture mode without a named session file.
55	  private let isDisabled: Bool
56	  /// Where an undecodable file is moved once, so a bug report has something to attach instead of the
57	  /// evidence being deleted.
58	  var quarantineURL: URL {
59	    url.deletingLastPathComponent().appendingPathComponent("session.corrupt.json")
60	  }
61	
62	  /// True once a file written by a NEWER schema has been read. Every write is then refused for the
63	  /// rest of the run — otherwise this build silently destroys a session it could not understand, and
64	  /// three build identities ship side by side, so that rollback is a real path rather than a
65	  /// hypothetical one.
66	  private(set) var writesDisabled = false
67	
68	  private let fileManager: FileManager
69	  private let logger = Logger(
70	    subsystem: "com.developwithstyle.workroom", category: "session")
71	  /// Encoding and the write happen here so neither runs on the main actor; only the capture does.
72	  private let queue = DispatchQueue(
73	    label: "com.developwithstyle.workroom.session", qos: .utility)
74	
75	  init(
76	    url: URL = SessionStore.defaultURL(), fileManager: FileManager = .default,
77	    isDisabled: Bool = false
78	  ) {
79	    self.url = url
80	    self.fileManager = fileManager
81	    self.isDisabled = isDisabled
82	  }
83	
84	  // MARK: Read
85	
86	  enum ReadOutcome: Equatable {
87	    /// Nothing usable — a fresh install, an unreadable file, or one this build cannot decode. The
88	    /// caller falls back to its cold-start path.
89	    case none
90	    case restored(SessionFile, SessionSanitizeReport)
91	    /// Written by a newer build: restore nothing, and `writesDisabled` is now true.
92	    case newerSchema
93	
94	    static func == (lhs: ReadOutcome, rhs: ReadOutcome) -> Bool {
95	      switch (lhs, rhs) {
96	      case (.none, .none), (.newerSchema, .newerSchema): return true
97	      case (.restored(let lf, let lr), .restored(let rf, let rr)):
98	        return lf.windows == rf.windows && lf.schemaVersion == rf.schemaVersion && lr == rr
99	      default: return false
100	      }
101	    }
102	  }
103	
104	  func read() -> ReadOutcome {
105	    guard !isDisabled, fileManager.fileExists(atPath: url.path) else { return .none }
106	
107	    // Refused BEFORE decoding: the element caps in `SessionLimits` bound how many things a file
108	    // describes, not how many bytes one of them spends.
109	    if let size = try? fileManager.attributesOfItem(atPath: url.path)[.size] as? Int,
110	      size > SessionLimits.maxFileBytes
111	    {
112	      logger.error("session file is \(size) bytes, over the limit — quarantining")
113	      quarantine()
114	      return .none
115	    }
116	
117	    guard let data = try? Data(contentsOf: url) else {
118	      logger.error("session file unreadable")
119	      return .none
120	    }
121	    guard !data.isEmpty else { return .none }
122	
123	    let decoder = JSONDecoder()
124	    decoder.dateDecodingStrategy = .iso8601
125	    guard let file = try? decoder.decode(SessionFile.self, from: data) else {
126	      logger.error("session file could not be decoded — quarantining")
127	      quarantine()
128	      return .none
129	    }
130	
131	    switch file.compatibility {
132	    case .newer:
133	      let message =
134	        "session file schema \(file.schemaVersion) is newer than "
135	        + "\(SessionFile.currentSchemaVersion) — not restoring, writes disabled for this run"
136	      logger.notice("\(message, privacy: .public)")
137	      writesDisabled = true
138	      return .newerSchema
139	    case .unreadable:
140	      logger.notice("session file schema \(file.schemaVersion) has no migration — discarding")
141	      return .none
142	    case .current:
143	      break
144	    }
145	
146	    let (sanitized, report) = file.sanitized()
147	    if !report.isEmpty {
148	      logger.notice("session file dropped entries — \(report.summary, privacy: .public)")
149	    }
150	    // A file whose windows all dropped is not a session. Saying so lets the caller take its
151	    // cold-start fallback instead of launching emptier than deleting the file would have.
152	    guard !sanitized.windows.isEmpty else { return .none }
153	    return .restored(sanitized, report)
154	  }
155	
156	  // MARK: Write
157	
158	  /// Persist off the main actor. Coalescing is the caller's job (see `AppStore+Session`).
159	  ///
160	  /// `completion` reports on the main actor whether the bytes actually reached disk. The caller needs
161	  /// it: it gates a write on "did this change since last time?", and treating a failed write as
162	  /// written would suppress every retry of the same state until something else changed.
163	  func write(_ file: SessionFile, completion: (@MainActor (Bool) -> Void)? = nil) {
164	    guard !isDisabled, !writesDisabled else {
165	      if let completion {
166	        DispatchQueue.main.async { MainActor.assumeIsolated { completion(false) } }
167	      }
168	      return
169	    }
170	    queue.async { [weak self] in
171	      let ok = self?.persist(file) ?? false
172	      guard let completion else { return }
173	      DispatchQueue.main.async { MainActor.assumeIsolated { completion(ok) } }
174	    }
175	  }
176	
177	  /// Persist before returning — the quit path, where the process may not survive long enough for an
178	  /// async write to land.
179	  @discardableResult
180	  func writeSynchronously(_ file: SessionFile) -> Bool {
181	    guard !isDisabled, !writesDisabled else { return false }
182	    return queue.sync { self.persist(file) }
183	  }
184	
185	  func clear() {
186	    guard !isDisabled else { return }
187	    queue.sync { try? self.fileManager.removeItem(at: self.url) }
188	  }
189	
190	  // MARK: Scrollback sidecars (issue #144)
191	
192	  /// One plain-text file per pane, beside `session.json`. Deliberately NOT inside it: that document
193	  /// is rewritten on every coalesced save, and a few hundred KB of terminal output per pane has no
194	  /// business riding along with the layout.
195	  var scrollbackDirectory: URL {
196	    url.deletingLastPathComponent().appendingPathComponent("scrollback", isDirectory: true)
197	  }
198	
199	  /// Rejects a key that could address anything outside the scrollback directory.
200	  ///
201	  /// The keys this app writes are `TabSession.key` UUID strings, which are filesystem-safe by
202	  /// construction — but `session.json` is a plain file a user (or anything running as them) can edit,
203	  /// and `URL.appendingPathComponent` does **not** normalise: a key of `../../../x` yields a path
204	  /// that escapes on access (measured). Since `readScrollback` *deletes* a file that fails
205	  /// validation, an unchecked key is an arbitrary-file-delete primitive at launch.
206	  ///
207	  /// A separator check rather than a strict UUID match, so the rule bites the actual hazard without
208	  /// making the key format part of the on-disk contract.
209	  nonisolated static func isSafeScrollbackKey(_ key: String) -> Bool {
210	    guard !key.isEmpty, key.count <= 128, !key.hasPrefix(".") else { return false }
211	    return !key.contains("/") && !key.contains(":") && !key.contains("\0")
212	  }
213	
214	  private func scrollbackURL(forTabKey key: String) -> URL? {
215	    guard Self.isSafeScrollbackKey(key) else {
216	      logger.error("refusing an unsafe scrollback key")
217	      return nil
218	    }
219	    return scrollbackDirectory.appendingPathComponent("\(key).txt")
220	  }
221	
222	  func writeScrollback(_ text: String, forTabKey key: String) {
223	    guard !isDisabled, !writesDisabled, !text.isEmpty else { return }
224	    guard let fileURL = scrollbackURL(forTabKey: key) else { return }
225	    do {
226	      // Owner-only, on the directory as well as the file: a sidecar is verbatim terminal output, so
227	      // it can hold whatever the user's shell printed — tokens, `env` dumps, connection strings. The
228	      // default 0644 would leave that readable by every other account on the machine.
229	      try fileManager.createDirectory(
230	        at: scrollbackDirectory, withIntermediateDirectories: true,
231	        attributes: [.posixPermissions: 0o700])
232	      try Data(text.utf8).write(to: fileURL, options: .atomic)
233	      // `.atomic` writes a temp file and renames, so the mode has to be set after the rename.
234	      try? fileManager.setAttributes([.posixPermissions: 0o600], ofItemAtPath: fileURL.path)
235	    } catch {
236	      // Best-effort like everything else here: a pane with no sidecar simply restores empty.
237	      logger.error("scrollback write failed: \(error.localizedDescription)")
238	    }
239	  }
240	
241	  /// The saved text for a pane, or nil when there is none, it is unreadable, or it fails validation.
242	  ///
243	  /// A file that fails validation is **deleted**: it would fail identically on every future launch,
244	  /// and unlike `session.json` a scrollback sidecar has no diagnostic value worth quarantining.
245	  func readScrollback(forTabKey key: String) -> String? {
246	    guard !isDisabled, let fileURL = scrollbackURL(forTabKey: key) else { return nil }
247	    guard fileManager.fileExists(atPath: fileURL.path) else { return nil }
248	
249	    if let size = try? fileManager.attributesOfItem(atPath: fileURL.path)[.size] as? Int,
250	      size > SessionLimits.maxScrollbackFileBytes
251	    {
252	      logger.notice("scrollback sidecar is \(size) bytes, over the limit — discarding")
253	      try? fileManager.removeItem(at: fileURL)
254	      return nil
255	    }
256	    guard let data = try? Data(contentsOf: fileURL) else { return nil }
257	    guard let text = String(data: data, encoding: .utf8) else {
258	      logger.notice("scrollback sidecar is not valid UTF-8 — discarding")
259	      try? fileManager.removeItem(at: fileURL)
260	      return nil
261	    }
262	    let cleaned = Self.strippingControlBytes(text)
263	    return cleaned.isEmpty ? nil : cleaned
264	  }
265	
266	  /// Drop sidecars for panes that are no longer in the session.
267	  ///
268	  /// Runs once after the write pass, unconditionally — including when every write failed. A pane
269	  /// whose capture is now empty wrote no sidecar, so its old one is removed here and yesterday's
270	  /// output cannot reappear under today's empty pane.
271	  func pruneScrollback(keeping keys: Set<String>) {
272	    guard !isDisabled else { return }
273	    guard
274	      let entries = try? fileManager.contentsOfDirectory(
275	        at: scrollbackDirectory, includingPropertiesForKeys: nil)
276	    else { return }
277	    for entry in entries where entry.pathExtension == "txt" {
278	      let key = entry.deletingPathExtension().lastPathComponent
279	      if !keys.contains(key) { try? fileManager.removeItem(at: entry) }
280	    }
281	  }
282	
283	  /// Remove C0 control bytes except newline, carriage return and tab.
284	  ///
285	  /// The captured text is rendered output, never raw PTY bytes, so it carries no escape sequences to
286	  /// begin with. This exists so a hand-edited sidecar cannot inject one and leave the parser
287	  /// mid-sequence on replay. CR is kept: the divider is CRLF.
288	  nonisolated static func strippingControlBytes(_ text: String) -> String {
289	    String(
290	      text.unicodeScalars.filter { scalar in
291	        scalar == "\n" || scalar == "\r" || scalar == "\t" || scalar.value >= 0x20
292	      })
293	  }
294	
295	  @discardableResult
296	  private func persist(_ file: SessionFile) -> Bool {
297	    let encoder = JSONEncoder()
298	    encoder.dateEncodingStrategy = .iso8601
299	    // Readable and diff-stable on purpose: "delete this file and relaunch" is a support instruction
300	    // a user can follow, and the file is something a bug report can usefully attach.
301	    encoder.outputFormatting = [.prettyPrinted, .sortedKeys]
302	
303	    guard let data = try? encoder.encode(file) else {
304	      logger.error("session snapshot could not be encoded")
305	      return false
306	    }
307	    do {
308	      // `Data.write(.atomic)` does NOT create intermediate directories, and the bundle-id
309	      // subdirectory does not exist on a first run — without this every write fails silently.
310	      try fileManager.createDirectory(
311	        at: url.deletingLastPathComponent(), withIntermediateDirectories: true)
312	      // Atomic: a reader sees the complete old document or the complete new one, never a partial
313	      // write from a process that died mid-save.
314	      try data.write(to: url, options: .atomic)
315	      return true
316	    } catch {
317	      logger.error("session snapshot could not be written: \(error.localizedDescription)")
318	      return false
319	    }
320	  }
321	
322	  /// Move a file this build cannot read aside — once. A prior quarantine is replaced rather than
323	  /// accumulating; the newest failure is the useful one.
324	  private func quarantine() {
325	    try? fileManager.removeItem(at: quarantineURL)
326	    do {
327	      try fileManager.moveItem(at: url, to: quarantineURL)
328	    } catch {
329	      // If it cannot even be moved, delete it — leaving it in place would fail the same way on
330	      // every launch forever.
331	      try? fileManager.removeItem(at: url)
332	    }
333	  }
334	}

3	/// Shared, app-wide project data: the project list plus everything derived from it that is
4	/// identical across windows — root branch/bookmark labels, the VCS/CI status cache, GitHub-CLI
5	/// availability, and the in-flight project busy set. Extracted from `AppStore` (issue #70) so that
6	/// multiple per-window `AppStore`s can share one project list while each keeps its own selection,
7	/// terminals, splits, history, and run state.
8	///
9	/// This first step is **storage-only and behaviour-preserving**: `AppStore` proxies these
10	/// properties straight through to here and re-publishes the store's `objectWillChange`, so the
11	/// single shared `AppStore` still behaves exactly as before. The CLI/load logic stays on `AppStore`
12	/// for now (it mutates these via the proxies); per-window construction and the multi-window wiring
13	/// land in a follow-up.
14	@MainActor
15	final class ProjectStore: ObservableObject {
16	  /// The shared instance used in production (every window's `AppStore` points at it). Tests
17	  /// construct an isolated `AppStore()`, which gets its own fresh `ProjectStore`, so they never
18	  /// pollute this singleton or each other.
19	  static let shared = ProjectStore()
20	
21	  /// The list of configured projects (from the CLI's `~/.config/workroom/config.json`). The one
22	  /// piece of state shared across all windows.
23	  @Published var projects: [Project] = []
24	
25	  /// Per-project resolved root branch/bookmark labels, hydrated asynchronously after each load.
26	  @Published var rootRefs: [Project.ID: RootRef] = [:]
27	
28	  /// Per-workroom (and per-root) VCS + CI status driving the ambient badges and the Changes panel
29	  /// (issue #24), keyed by `SidebarID`. Resolved app-side, best-effort/"last checked". Shared so two
30	  /// windows showing the same workroom report a consistent badge and don't double the probes.
31	  @Published var workroomStatuses: [SidebarID: WorkroomStatus] = [:]
32	
33	  /// Whether the GitHub CLI is usable for the PR/CI probes (machine-global). Optimistic default so
34	  /// no warning flashes before the first check.
35	  @Published var githubCLIStatus: GitHubCLIStatus = .available
36	
37	  /// Owns the `gh auth status` probe: its freshness clock AND its single-flight, so N windows share
38	  /// one `gh` and the staleness check can't interleave with the write the way a bare timestamp on
39	  /// this class did. `githubCLIStatus` above is the SwiftUI-observable mirror of what it decided.
40	  ///
41	  /// A `var` purely so tests can swap in an instance with millisecond TTLs; production never
42	  /// reassigns it.
43	  var ghAuthCache = GitHubAuthCache()
44	
45	  /// Project paths with an in-flight create/delete (for per-row progress + disabling).
46	  @Published var busyProjects: Set<String> = []
47	
48	  /// Target ids of workrooms whose create is still in flight — from the "created" event until the
49	  /// create flow ends (issue #116). A workroom here must not be deleted: its setup script is running
50	  /// against the worktree. Shared across windows so a delete from ANY window is blocked, not just the
51	  /// creating one.
52	  @Published var creatingWorkrooms: Set<TerminalTarget.ID> = []
53	
54	  /// Sidebar rows with a commit in flight, for the per-row button state.
55	  ///
56	  /// Shared across windows for the reason `creatingWorkrooms` is: `AppStore` is per WINDOW, but
57	  /// `JJSnapshotGate` and the `index.lock` contention it exists to prevent are per PROCESS. Held on
58	  /// the window's own store, a second window's 15s sweep, FSEvents lane and Refresh button all saw an
59	  /// empty set and kept probing a repo mid-write.
60	  @Published var committingTargets: Set<SidebarID> = []
61	
62	  /// How many commits are in flight against each project root, which is what the read lanes actually
63	  /// have to stand clear of.
64	  ///

17	  /// Coalescing window. Long enough that a burst of layout edits costs one write.

31	  private let store: SessionStore
32	  private let debounce: TimeInterval

45	  /// process, and a collision would silently suppress a write the user needs.

3	/// The on-disk shape of a saved session — the open panels, split layouts, and windows restored on
4	/// the next launch (issue #46). Written by `SessionStore` to
5	/// `Application Support/Workroom/<bundle id>/session.json`.
6	///
7	/// **Every type here is a hand-written mirror.** No runtime type (`PaneLayout`, `TerminalTab`,
8	/// `SidebarID`, the content descriptors) gains `Codable`, so the file format is never hostage to an
9	/// internal field rename — the same stored-data-contract rule `RunConfig` carries in
10	/// `DefaultsKeys.swift`. The field names below ARE the contract; renaming one silently invalidates
11	/// every user's saved session.
12	///
13	/// # Versioning rule — read before bumping `schemaVersion`
14	///
15	/// **Additive changes NEVER bump `schemaVersion`.** Adding a tab kind, or adding an optional field,
16	/// is additive. Only a breaking reshape bumps.
17	///
18	/// This is what makes the lossy decoding below load-bearing rather than decorative: a Nightly build
19	/// writes a fifth tab kind, the user rolls back to stable, and stable drops that one tab while
20	/// restoring everything else. Bump the version for an additive kind and the whole file is discarded
21	/// before the lossy path ever runs — deleting every user's session for no reason.
22	///
23	/// The same split the app already draws between versioning a key (`inspector.layout.v2`) and
24	/// reconciling a shape (`AppStore.reconcileInspectorState`): version to discard, reconcile to keep.
25	///
26	/// A **newer** `schemaVersion` is read-only: restore nothing AND write nothing for that run, or an
27	/// older build silently destroys a newer one's session on its next save. Three build identities ship
28	/// side by side (Workroom, Workroom Dev, Workroom Nightly), so that rollback is a real path.
29	///
30	/// # What is deliberately absent
31	///
32	/// - **The PTY and child processes.** A restored terminal is a fresh login shell in the remembered
33	///   directory; the process it was running is gone. (Its *text* does come back — scrollback lives in
34	///   sidecar files beside this document, never inside it. See `SessionStore` and issue #144.)
35	/// - **Run tabs.** Restoring one would resurrect a dev server with no `AppStore.RunState` behind it —
36	///   an untracked process orphaned on its port, the failure `WindowRegistry.runOwner(for:excluding:)`
37	///   and issue #7 exist to prevent. `Defaults[.runCommands]` already survives, and `RunConfig.autoRun`
38	///   is the deliberate opt-in.
39	/// - **`liveTitle` / `progressActive` / activity pulses.** Display state about a process that no
40	///   longer exists. Excluding them is also what keeps the save digest stable: a terminal animating
41	///   its title produces a byte-identical snapshot, so it costs a comparison and no disk write.
42	/// - **Navigation history.** Its entries key on tab ids, which restore re-mints by design.

47	/// not decoration: restore materialises every target's tab models eagerly (the sidebar's terminal
48	/// subtree renders from them), so a hostile or corrupt file could otherwise allocate tens of
49	/// thousands of views before the first frame. Anything dropped is logged — silent truncation reads
50	/// as full coverage.
51	enum SessionLimits {
52	  static let maxWindows = 8
53	  /// Workroom's whole point is managing many workrooms, so this has to sit above real usage rather
54	  /// than above a guess: 20 was tight enough that a heavy user would silently lose targets on every
55	  /// relaunch. **Enforced at capture as well as at read** (`AppStore.captureWindowSession`), so the
56	  /// app can never author a file it will later truncate.

58	  static let maxTabsPerTarget = 20

60	  /// cap is what stops a hand-edited file recursing `materialize` into the stack.

62	  /// Nesting depth refused **during decoding**, before a tree is built at all.
63	  ///

65	  /// far too late, because `init(from:)` recurses per level as it decodes. A deeply nested file would

67	  /// crash on every launch with no way out. Throwing here drops one element through `@Lossy` instead.
68	  /// Well above `maxSplitDepth` plus the outer document's own coding path, so no real file trips it.
69	  static let maxDecodeDepth = 64

71	  ///

112	      } catch {
113	        _ = try? container.decode(AnyElement.self)
114	      }
115	      // Belt and braces: if neither the decode nor the skip advanced the cursor, stop rather than
116	      // spin forever on a container shape we did not anticipate.
117	      if container.currentIndex == indexBefore { break }
118	    }
119	    wrappedValue = decoded
120	  }

141	/// The Codable mirror of `PaneLayout`, generic over its leaf address (a tab key, or a target-id
142	/// string for the workroom split). Hand-written with an explicit `kind` discriminator so the on-disk
143	/// format is a contract THIS file owns, not whatever Swift synthesises for an indirect enum with
144	/// associated values.
145	///
146	/// `PaneLayout`'s per-split `UUID` is deliberately NOT persisted: it addresses a divider during a
147	/// drag and nothing refers to it across a launch. `materialize` mints a fresh one.
148	indirect enum LayoutNode<Leaf: Codable & Hashable & Sendable>: Codable, Hashable, Sendable {
149	  case leaf(Leaf)
150	  case split(orientation: String, ratio: Double, first: LayoutNode, second: LayoutNode)
151	
152	  static var horizontal: String { "horizontal" }
153	  static var vertical: String { "vertical" }
154	
155	  private enum CodingKeys: String, CodingKey {
156	    case kind, leaf, orientation, ratio, first, second
157	  }
158	  private enum Kind: String, Codable {
159	    case leaf, split
160	  }
161	
162	  init(from decoder: Decoder) throws {
163	    // Refused BEFORE recursing. `sanitized()`'s `maxSplitDepth` check cannot help here — it inspects
164	    // a tree that decoding has already built, and building it is the stack hazard. Each nesting level
165	    // adds a `first`/`second` key to the coding path, so the path length is the live depth.
166	    guard decoder.codingPath.count <= SessionLimits.maxDecodeDepth else {
167	      throw DecodingError.dataCorrupted(
168	        DecodingError.Context(
169	          codingPath: decoder.codingPath,
170	          debugDescription: "split tree nested deeper than \(SessionLimits.maxDecodeDepth)"))
171	    }
172	    let container = try decoder.container(keyedBy: CodingKeys.self)
173	    switch try container.decode(Kind.self, forKey: .kind) {
174	    case .leaf:
175	      self = .leaf(try container.decode(Leaf.self, forKey: .leaf))
176	    case .split:
177	      self = .split(
178	        orientation: try container.decode(String.self, forKey: .orientation),
179	        ratio: try container.decode(Double.self, forKey: .ratio),
180	        first: try container.decode(LayoutNode.self, forKey: .first),
181	        second: try container.decode(LayoutNode.self, forKey: .second))
182	    }
183	  }
184	
185	  func encode(to encoder: Encoder) throws {
186	    var container = encoder.container(keyedBy: CodingKeys.self)
187	    switch self {
188	    case .leaf(let leaf):
189	      try container.encode(Kind.leaf, forKey: .kind)
190	      try container.encode(leaf, forKey: .leaf)
191	    case .split(let orientation, let ratio, let first, let second):
192	      try container.encode(Kind.split, forKey: .kind)
193	      try container.encode(orientation, forKey: .orientation)
194	      try container.encode(ratio, forKey: .ratio)
195	      try container.encode(first, forKey: .first)
196	      try container.encode(second, forKey: .second)
197	    }
198	  }
199	
200	  /// Every leaf address in reading order — the counterpart of `PaneLayout.tabIDs`, used to validate
201	  /// a decoded tree against the tabs that actually survived.
202	  var leaves: [Leaf] {
203	    switch self {
204	    case .leaf(let leaf): return [leaf]
205	    case .split(_, _, let first, let second): return first.leaves + second.leaves
206	    }
207	  }
208	
209	  /// Depth of the deepest split, so a hand-edited tree can be rejected before `materialize` walks it.
210	  var depth: Int {
211	    switch self {
212	    case .leaf: return 1
213	    case .split(_, _, let first, let second): return 1 + max(first.depth, second.depth)
214	    }
215	  }
216	}

218	extension LayoutNode {
219	  /// Runtime tree → snapshot tree. `address` maps a runtime leaf to its persisted key; a leaf that
220	  /// maps to nil is dropped and its parent collapses to the surviving sibling — the same collapse
221	  /// rule as `PaneLayout.removingLeaf`.
222	  ///
223	  /// Returns nil when fewer than two leaves survive, mirroring `materialize`: a lone leaf is not a
224	  /// split, and writing one would put a shape in the file that the live model cannot hold. Excluding
225	  /// a run tab from a two-pane split is exactly this case.
226	  static func capture<L: Hashable>(
227	    _ layout: PaneLayout<L>, address: (L) -> Leaf?
228	  ) -> LayoutNode? {
229	    guard let tree = captureNode(layout, address: address) else { return nil }
230	    guard case .split = tree else { return nil }
231	    return tree
232	  }
233	
234	  private static func captureNode<L: Hashable>(
235	    _ layout: PaneLayout<L>, address: (L) -> Leaf?
236	  ) -> LayoutNode? {
237	    switch layout {
238	    case .leaf(let id):
239	      return address(id).map { .leaf($0) }
240	    case .split(_, let orientation, let ratio, let first, let second):
241	      let capturedFirst = captureNode(first, address: address)
242	      let capturedSecond = captureNode(second, address: address)
243	      switch (capturedFirst, capturedSecond) {
244	      case (let first?, let second?):
245	        return .split(
246	          orientation: orientation == .horizontal ? horizontal : vertical,
247	          ratio: Double(ratio), first: first, second: second)
248	      // A split with one surviving child is not a split — it IS that child (`PaneLayout`'s
249	      // "a lone leaf is not a split" invariant, enforced at the boundary rather than left to callers).
250	      case (let only?, nil), (nil, let only?):
251	        return only
252	      case (nil, nil):
253	        return nil
254	      }
255	    }
256	  }
257	
258	  /// Snapshot tree → runtime tree. `resolve` maps a persisted key to a live leaf; unresolvable leaves
259	  /// collapse into their sibling. Returns nil when fewer than two leaves survive, so a caller can
260	  /// never be handed a one-leaf "split".
261	  func materialize<L: Hashable>(_ resolve: (Leaf) -> L?) -> PaneLayout<L>? {
262	    guard let tree = materializeNode(resolve, depth: 0) else { return nil }
263	    guard case .split = tree else { return nil }
264	    return tree
265	  }
266	
267	  private func materializeNode<L: Hashable>(
268	    _ resolve: (Leaf) -> L?, depth: Int
269	  ) -> PaneLayout<L>? {
270	    guard depth < SessionLimits.maxSplitDepth else { return nil }
271	    switch self {
272	    case .leaf(let key):
273	      return resolve(key).map { .leaf($0) }
274	    case .split(let orientation, let ratio, let first, let second):
275	      guard let resolvedOrientation = Self.orientation(from: orientation) else { return nil }
276	      let resolvedFirst = first.materializeNode(resolve, depth: depth + 1)
277	      let resolvedSecond = second.materializeNode(resolve, depth: depth + 1)
278	      switch (resolvedFirst, resolvedSecond) {
279	      case (let first?, let second?):
280	        return .split(
281	          id: UUID(), orientation: resolvedOrientation,
282	          ratio: PaneRatio.sanitize(CGFloat(ratio)), first: first, second: second)
283	      case (let only?, nil), (nil, let only?):
284	        return only
285	      case (nil, nil):
286	        return nil
287	      }
288	    }
289	  }
290	
291	  /// An unrecognised orientation rejects the split (its tabs survive as solo panes) rather than
292	  /// guessing a layout the user never chose.
293	  private static func orientation(from raw: String) -> SplitOrientation? {
294	    switch raw {
295	    case horizontal: return .horizontal
296	    case vertical: return .vertical
297	    default: return nil
298	    }
299	  }
300	}
